pillars.name: Typing
pillars.function_text: The brain coordinates attention, memory, decisions and quick reactions. In space, short sleep and isolation can lower its performance without the astronaut noticing.
pillars.hazard_text: Isolation and an irregular schedule: short sleep lowers attention without you noticing.
pillars.limits_text: Typing as a sign of fatigue has little evidence behind it (one small study). We never read what you write, only the rhythm.

sources.citation: Van Dongen et al. (2003), The cumulative cost of additional wakefulness, Sleep 26(2):117–126

pillars.name: Heart
pillars.function_text: The heart pumps the blood that carries oxygen and nutrients through the whole body. In microgravity, fluids rise towards the head, and on return you may feel dizzy when standing up.
pillars.hazard_text: Altered gravity: the heart works less and becomes deconditioned.
pillars.limits_text: The thresholds are not published for astronauts; they are derived. We compare against your in-flight normal, not the one from Earth.

sources.citation: NASA HRP — Risk of Cardiovascular Adaptations

pillars.name: Sentinel
pillars.function_text: The immune system defends the body against viruses, bacteria and abnormal cells. In flight, stress, disrupted sleep and radiation throw it off balance.
pillars.hazard_text: Radiation and the closed environment: stress and shared space weaken the body's defences.
pillars.limits_text: The algorithm cannot tell the type of infection and can give false alarms. It was validated on civilians, not on astronauts.

sources.citation: Alavi et al. (2022), Real-time alerting system for COVID-19 and other stress events using wearable data, Nature Medicine 28:175–184
Rooney et al. (2019), Herpes Virus Reactivation in Astronauts During Spaceflight, Frontiers in Microbiology 10:16
NASA HRP — Risk of Altered Immune Response

pillars.name: Loading
pillars.function_text: Bones support the body and protect the organs, and muscles produce movement; both are maintained by loading. Without gravity and without exercise, weight-bearing bones lose 1–1.5% of their density per month; with daily resistance exercise (ARED), about 0.3–0.6%.
pillars.hazard_text: Altered gravity: without the body's weight, bones and muscles lose mass.
pillars.limits_text: The effect of splitting exercise into sessions has been shown only in animals. Bone density is estimated, not measured.

sources.citation: NASA HRP (2024), Evidence Report: Risk of Bone Fracture due to Spaceflight-induced Changes to Bone
Robling et al. (2002), J Bone Miner Res 17(8):1545–1554
